Envoys & Diplomacy

The Sublime Porte (Bâbıâli)

‘The envoy of Lechistan has not yet arrived’ – the hero of the best-loved Polish–Turkish legend is the grand vizier, and the gate of his office stands right here.

Theme
Envoys & Diplomacy
District
Fatih
Period
1677–1678
Visiting
Seen from outside

The story

Behind this gate the grand viziers held office – among them Kara Mustafa, with whom the Polish envoy Jan Gniński wrangled in 1677 and 1678.

Bâbıâli, the Sublime Porte, was the grand vizier's seat, and its name came to stand for the Ottoman government itself. Gniński described his way to the vizier: through narrow streets, then uphill to a gate ‘just like the Kraków Castle’ and on to the Divan hall. The talks dragged on for months and almost every Polish demand was refused. They were probably held on this site, though it is not known exactly when the viziers settled here for good. Nothing from that time survives: the present gate, from Mahmud II's reign, now fronts the Governorship of Istanbul.

How to visit

The best view is from the pavement by the Alay Köşkü, the pavilion set in the wall of Gülhane Park on Alemdar Caddesi, about 100 m from the Gülhane stop of the T1 tram. Across the street stands the marble gate: a broad rounded arch under wide eaves, with an inscription and the sultan's tughra above, and niches and fountains at the sides. It is a working government office, so the gate is enjoyed from outside.
